grades.title: Grade 9 - Foundations
goals: Build curiosity about human behavior and mental health
Start habit tracking and observation skills

psychTopics: What is psychology? Branches (clinical, cognitive, social, I-O)
projects: Behavior journal (2 weeks): triggers -> behaviors -> outcomes
Mini research: design a survey for study habits (10+ responses)
Presentation: one psychology field + one real job

skills: Digital literacy and safe online research
activities: Join or start a psychology club
Volunteer 10-20 hours (community center, tutoring, elder care)
Watch an intro series (CrashCourse Psychology) and take notes
Interview a counselor/therapist: "What do you do weekly?"
milestones: Write one 2-3 page psychology topic report
Create a one-page career map: education -> job -> employers
recommendations: Focus on observation, empathy, health science, and accurate note-taking.
Build one small behavior journal project and one presentation about a psychology career.
Practice separating facts, feelings, thoughts, and behavior in everyday examples.
applicationEvidence: Short report on one psychology topic.
nextSteps: Choose one psychology field to follow for the year.
Ask a counselor or teacher about school psychology electives.

grades.title: Grade 10 - Brain & Behavior Systems
goals: Understand brain systems that impact behavior

projects: Sleep study: log 14 days -> chart outcomes

activities: Volunteer: youth mentoring or crisis-support training (age-appropriate)
Join science fair with a behavior topic
Start a basic portfolio folder (reports + reflections)
milestones: Complete a small survey study (20+ responses)
recommendations: Strengthen biology, writing, and early data interpretation.
Use sleep, stress, attention, and social influence as safe applied topics.
Begin comparing clinical, research, UX, school, and workplace psychology paths.
nextSteps: Track one behavior-health question for two weeks.
Save three possible internship or summer program ideas.
studyFocus: Charts, survey results, and simple interpretation.

grades.title: Grade 11 - Research & Applied Psychology
goals: Learn research methods and ethics deeper

projects: Design an experiment (simple): hypothesis -> variables -> procedure
Literature review (5 credible sources) on one topic

activities: Volunteer at hospital/community mental health org (if permitted)
Shadow a counselor, OT, social worker, or clinic admin
Try R or Python basics (optional but powerful)
recommendations: Prioritize AP Psychology, statistics, research methods, and ethical reasoning.
Start supervised exposure through school, community, lab, hospital, or nonprofit settings where allowed.
Build a resume and portfolio around evidence, not vague interest.
nextSteps: Choose one primary career path and two backups.
Prepare questions for a psychology professional interview.
studyFocus: Correlation, causation, and limits of evidence.

grades.title: Grade 12 - College & Career Launch
goals: Finalize track (clinical, research, I-O, UX, etc.)
Build a portfolio and internship plan
Understand education requirements for each role

psychTopics: Career map: BA/BS vs MA/MS vs PhD/PsyD

milestones: Pick a primary pathway and 2 backups
Have 10 employers saved with entry roles
recommendations: Finalize a school and career launch plan with realistic education requirements.
Polish three portfolio artifacts and connect each to a career path.
Prepare applications with ethics, boundaries, evidence, and fit clearly stated.
nextSteps: Save ten target employers or programs.
Apply for internships or summer programs.
studyFocus: BA/BS, MA/MS, PhD, PsyD, and licensure differences.

tracks.name: Clinical (PsyD/PhD)
notes: Most clinical psychologist roles require doctoral training + licensure

tracks.name: Counseling / Therapy (MA/MS)
notes: Often fastest path into direct counseling roles

tracks.name: Industrial-Organizational (MA/MS/PhD)
notes: Strong corporate demand; heavy on measurement and data

tracks.name: UX / Human Factors (MA/MS/PhD)
notes: High demand in tech; research skills matter most

careerPaths.title: Clinical Psychologist
careerPaths.summary: Assess, diagnose, and treat mental and emotional disorders using interviews, tests, and therapy methods.

careerPaths.title: UX Researcher
careerPaths.summary: Study how people interact with products and systems; run studies to improve design and usability.

careerPaths.title: Industrial-Organizational Psychologist
careerPaths.summary: Use psychology and data to improve hiring, leadership, teamwork, and organizational performance.
educationTypical: MA/MS or PhD in I-O Psychology

careerPaths.title: Behavioral Scientist
careerPaths.summary: Apply behavioral science to improve decisions, products, health outcomes, and policy.

careerPaths.title: Government / Behavioral Analysis (Pathway)
careerPaths.summary: Behavioral science roles exist across government; some paths require becoming an agent first (varies).

tools.title: Bias Checker
tools.summary: Identify confirmation, availability, anchoring, overconfidence, attribution, and loss-aversion risks in a psychology or behavioral health decision.
tools.why: Bias checks protect the learner from treating first impressions as evidence.
uses: Review a decision or case note.

tools.title: Decision Quality Review
tools.summary: Review a psychology-related choice for goal clarity, evidence quality, uncertainty, risk, reversibility, and next action.
tools.why: Behavioral health decisions improve when the learner can show what is known, unknown, and reversible.

tools.title: Behavioral Survey Builder
tools.summary: Design ethical surveys for school projects, study habits, wellbeing routines, motivation, or career interests.
tools.why: Good survey design keeps questions clear, consent-aware, and limited to appropriate learning use.

tools.title: Cognitive Distortion Analyzer
tools.summary: Learn to recognize thinking patterns such as all-or-nothing thinking, catastrophizing, mind reading, labeling, and should statements.
tools.why: Recognizing thinking patterns supports reflection and communication without diagnosing anyone.
uses: Rewrite it as a balanced observation.

tools.title: Psychology Learning Plan Builder
tools.summary: Turn a grade, course, or career goal into a study plan with topics, projects, milestones, and review checkpoints.
tools.why: A learning plan connects psychology content to practical evidence.
uses: Choose current grade or school stage.
Pick one topic and one project.
Set a milestone and review date.

tools.title: Reflection Prompt Builder
tools.summary: Create prompts for observation, emotion, behavior, assumptions, evidence, ethics, and next action.
tools.why: Structured reflection helps a learner build insight while staying inside educational boundaries.

tools.title: Case Study Analyzer
tools.summary: Analyze educational case studies by context, behavior, evidence, alternative explanations, bias risks, and ethical boundaries.
tools.why: Case analysis trains careful reasoning without jumping to diagnosis.

tools.title: Career Readiness Self-Assessment
tools.summary: Check readiness across coursework, skills, projects, internships, applications, and professional boundaries.
tools.why: Readiness should be based on evidence the learner can show.
uses: Match evidence to a target path.
Choose the next gap to close.

tools.title: Ethics Boundary Review
tools.summary: Review consent, privacy, scope, safety, referral, supervision, and respectful language before psychology-related work.
tools.why: Psychology and behavioral health work must protect people and avoid overclaiming.

tools.title: Behavior Scenario Simulator
tools.summary: Explore possible outcomes of school, career, case, or communication choices using assumptions, risks, supports, and alternatives.
tools.why: Scenario thinking helps the learner compare options without pretending to predict people perfectly.

sectors.title: Gaming & Media
howToApply: Search official career pages using psychology, behavioral health, research assistant, UX research, people analytics, program assistant, and internship keywords.
Save the role title, requirements, deadline, and application link.
Match each application to one portfolio project, one skill, and one education milestone.
applicationEvidence: One psychology or behavioral health project.
Reflection on ethics, privacy, and boundaries.

pipeline.why: Focus improves decisions and faster progress.
Projects > claims. Show skills in action.
Treat the job hunt like a research loop.

portfolioIdeas: Behavior change plan (health) with outcome tracking
Mini experiment (attention, sleep, stress) with ethics notes

mental_health_counselor.title: Substance Abuse, Behavioral Disorder, and Mental Health Counselors
mental_health_counselor.notes: Counseling pathway (role names vary by state licensure).

cards.title: Career Paths
cards.summary: Compare psychology, cognitive science, research, UX, organizational, healthcare, government, and AI-aligned career directions.
cards.whyThisMatters: A clear path helps the learner choose school, tools, projects, internships, and application evidence without guessing.
useThisInPractice: Pick one primary path and two backup paths.
Compare required education, experience, and portfolio signals.
Use Core career cards to decide what evidence to build next.
details: Clinical and counseling paths often require graduate education and licensure.
Research paths need methods, statistics, lab experience, and writing.
UX, product, people analytics, and behavioral science paths need research evidence and communication.
recommendedActions: Pick one project that proves readiness.

cards.title: Companies
cards.summary: Review employer sectors and example organizations connected to psychology, behavioral science, UX research, healthcare, consulting, government, media, and AI.
cards.whyThisMatters: Company research turns a general interest into real opportunity targets, role language, and application timing.
useThisInPractice: Save companies by sector.
Match each company to one career path and one portfolio project.
Use official career pages before outreach or applications.
details: Company research belongs under employer sectors, target teams, official career pages, and role requirements.
The learner should compare healthcare, research, technology, consulting, government, education, and media organizations.
recommendedActions: Match each to one role type.

cards.title: Internships
cards.summary: Plan internships, labs, observation hours, assistant roles, and supervised experience that build credible career evidence.
cards.whyThisMatters: Internships and supervised roles convert learning into verified practice, references, and portfolio proof.
useThisInPractice: Identify internship categories by path: lab, clinic, school, HR, UX, public health, product, or research.
Track deadlines, prerequisites, supervision rules, and school-credit requirements.
Write a reflection after each shadowing, lab, or internship experience.
details: Useful internship categories include research assistant, behavioral health program support, school support, UX research, people analytics, public health, and community education.
Some settings require age, background check, training, or supervision rules.
recommendedActions: Prepare a resume and project proof.
Ask about supervision and allowed duties.

cards.title: Start a Company
cards.summary: Explore how cognitive science and psychology can become a focused service, education product, assessment workflow, research support offer, or software tool.
cards.whyThisMatters: Founder work needs a narrow audience, ethical boundary, repeatable workflow, and measurable outcome before growth.
useThisInPractice: Choose one audience: students, schools, clinics, teams, workplaces, creators, researchers, or product teams.
Define what the company will do and what it will refuse to do outside scope.
Build one small portfolio proof before offering the service.
details: Founder ideas must stay within education, coaching, research support, analytics, or workflow support unless licensed clinical authority exists.
Good offers are narrow, ethical, measurable, and referral-aware.

cards.title: Business Models
cards.summary: Compare service, coaching, school program, research support, analytics, dashboard, content, and software models for applied cognitive work.
cards.whyThisMatters: A business model makes the user clarify who is served, what is delivered, how quality is protected, and how outcomes are reviewed.
useThisInPractice: Choose one delivery model before designing features or services.
Define pricing, support, quality review, privacy boundaries, and referral rules.
Tie the model to a career path, tool workflow, and portfolio project.
details: Possible models include workshops, school programs, research support, survey analysis, portfolio coaching, behavior-change education, and software dashboards.
Each model needs privacy, consent, quality review, and referral boundaries.
recommendedActions: Create an ethics and privacy checklist.

cards.title: Certifications
cards.summary: Track credentials, certificates, coursework, supervised requirements, and scope boundaries that support psychology-adjacent readiness.
cards.whyThisMatters: Credentials can strengthen readiness, but they must not be confused with licensure, diagnosis authority, or clinical scope.
useThisInPractice: Record each certification with issuer, date, renewal, and role relevance.
Separate certificates from licenses and supervised clinical authority.
Connect every credential to a portfolio project or internship requirement.
details: Certificates can support readiness but are not the same as licensure.
Track issuer, expiration, renewal, scope, and role relevance.
recommendedActions: Separate certificate, degree, license, and supervised experience.

cards.title: Portfolio Projects
cards.summary: Build evidence through survey studies, usability studies, behavior-change plans, literature reviews, dashboards, and ethics-aware case analyses.
cards.whyThisMatters: Projects make skills inspectable and help schools, employers, and collaborators understand what the learner can actually do.
useThisInPractice: Keep each project tied to a career path and a Core concept.
Include question, method, ethics note, result, limitation, and next action.
Use report export to turn saved work into a professional summary.
details: Strong projects include survey studies, literature reviews, usability studies, behavior-change plans, case analyses, dashboards, and ethics reviews.
Every project should show question, method, evidence, limitation, and next step.
recommendedActions: Add an ethics note to each.
Tie each project to a career path.

cards.title: School Roadmap
cards.summary: Connect grade-level and post-secondary learning to psychology topics, projects, milestones, internships, and career paths.
cards.whyThisMatters: A school roadmap helps the learner choose classes, projects, activities, and application evidence in the right order.
useThisInPractice: Review the current grade or school stage.
Pick one project and one activity for the current term.
Map courses and milestones to a career path before applying.
details: Grade-level planning should connect classes, psychology topics, activities, projects, milestones, and applications.
Post-secondary planning should compare undergraduate, graduate, licensure, research, and applied industry paths.
recommendedActions: Pick one project and one application milestone.

cards.title: Skills Builder
cards.summary: Develop research design, statistics, ethics, communication, empathy, data tools, survey design, dashboards, and applied analysis skills.
cards.whyThisMatters: Skills become useful when they are practiced through projects and connected to real career or school evidence.
useThisInPractice: Choose one core skill and one tool skill.
Practice the skill through a small project.
Save the evidence to a portfolio or report.
details: Core psychology skills include observation, ethics, communication, research design, statistics, case reasoning, survey design, and reflective practice.
Tool skills should support psychology work, not become the purpose of the app.
recommendedActions: Pick one concept skill and one evidence skill.

cards.title: Application Prep
cards.summary: Prepare resumes, personal statements, cover notes, portfolios, interview answers, school applications, internships, and job applications.
cards.whyThisMatters: Application prep turns learning into a clear story with evidence, fit, boundaries, and next steps.
useThisInPractice: Create one resume or application version per role or program.
Use the opportunity description to select proof points.
Track submissions, follow-ups, interviews, and outcomes.
details: Application prep includes role research, resume, cover note, personal statement, interview stories, portfolio evidence, references, and follow-up tracking.
Each application should show fit, boundaries, and evidence.
recommendedActions: Choose a target role or program.
Track submission, follow-up, interview, and result.

cards.title: Behavioral Health Learning Guide
cards.summary: Use Core psychology knowledge to choose what to study next across behavior, cognition, emotion, ethics, and career readiness.
cards.whyThisMatters: The AI surface should point the learner toward psychology and behavioral health learning, not generic automation.
prompts: What psychology topic am I struggling to understand right now?
Which behavioral health concept connects to my current goal?
What should I study next based on the Core roadmap?
outputGoal: A related career, tool, or portfolio action.
guardrails: Education only; not diagnosis or treatment.
Escalate urgent safety or clinical concerns to qualified professionals.

cards.title: Case Reflection Coach
cards.summary: Structure a behavioral health case reflection around context, behavior, evidence, bias risk, ethics, and next questions.
cards.whyThisMatters: Good psychology reasoning separates observation from interpretation and keeps boundaries visible.
guardrails: Do not label, diagnose, or recommend treatment from limited information.
Use supervised or professional review for real clinical situations.

cards.title: Psychology Career Readiness Coach
cards.summary: Connect school stage, skills, portfolio projects, companies, internships, certifications, and applications to a psychology path.
cards.whyThisMatters: A learner needs a practical path from study to evidence to applications.
prompts: What grade or school stage am I in?
Which psychology career path interests me most?
What proof should I build before applying?
outputGoal: A company, internship, or application prep target.
guardrails: Licensure and clinical authority vary by jurisdiction.
Always verify program and employer requirements from official sources.
